title: T-037 retrieval seam and GO
summary: Claude reviewed T-034, T-035, and the exclusive seam assignment through Cole and issued T-037 GO with measured quality, latency, degradation, and production-enable conditions.
evidence: T-037 owns retrieval candidate acquisition, fusion, ranking, feature-flag fallback, and rollback inside retrieveChunks() and new retrieval-only helpers in query.js.
T-037 must not change provider selection, history rewriting, citation rendering, confidenceForChunks(), or needsReview.
T-042 exclusively owns the provider-selection branch inside answerFromContext() in embed.js and has completed that package.
T-039 exclusively owns the history-aware rewrite stage before retrieveChunks() in askQuestion() and must enter through the T-042 queue.
T-038 owns citation metadata joining and may change only publicSources() and persisted chunks_used citation fields in query.js.
T-037 and T-039 may not edit query.js concurrently, and the T-037 receipt must identify every function changed.
Missing sqlite-vec must degrade to FTS5 and then lexical, log once, and fail no request.
hit@5 and MRR must not regress in any category, concept questions must improve, retrieval p95 must be at most 300 ms, and p99 at most 800 ms.
The five unsupported-topic cases may add no unsupported claim versus baseline.
limitations: The feature flag defaults off and cannot be enabled in production until T-046 passes the mandatory legal-refusal and approved no-answer gates.
